subject: Ward 5 Neighborhood Listening Session
overview: The City Council held a listening session for Ward 5 residents to identify neighborhood priorities and concerns. Key discussions centered on traffic calming, infrastructure maintenance, and public safety policy.

items.title: Opening Remarks and Meeting Format
items.summary: Councilors Callahan and Tseng introduced the listening session as an open forum to gather feedback on local issues and neighborhood improvements.

items.title: Resident Public Comment
items.summary: Residents raised concerns regarding affordability, traffic safety on Main and Winchester Streets, tree canopy loss, and the impact of new zoning on historical neighborhoods.

items.title: Remote Participant Feedback
items.summary: Zoom participants echoed concerns about motorcycle noise, water quality, gas leaks, and the need for better snow removal near Tufts Park.

items.title: Traffic Calming and Enforcement
items.summary: Councilors addressed the city's limited traffic engineering staff and discussed using infrastructure design, such as speed humps and street bump-outs, as an alternative to police-led enforcement.

items.title: Noise Ordinance and Heavy Trucking
items.summary: Councilor Tseng detailed a proposed update to the noise ordinance to address loud exhaust and outlined plans to lobby the state for waivers to restrict heavy trucks from cut-through streets.

items.title: Welcoming City Ordinance and ICE
items.summary: The Council reviewed legislative efforts to prevent local police from collaborating with ICE and upcoming committee work to strengthen resident protections.

items.title: Tree Management and Vacant Buildings
items.summary: Councilors highlighted the appointment of a new tree warden, upcoming volunteer planting initiatives, and a new ordinance to penalize landlords who keep properties vacant or poorly maintained.

items.title: Snow Removal and Park Maintenance
items.summary: The Council discussed the systemic underfunding and equipment shortages that hampered snow removal last winter and acknowledged a lack of administrative transparency regarding plans for Tufts Park.

items.title: Air Traffic Patterns
items.summary: Representative Micah Kesselman provided an update on a reopened investigation into flight patterns over Medford and efforts to lobby the FAA for changes.
